security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives from documentation tables, prompt examples, and code fences. Confirmed risks are intended CLI execution, global package installation, authentication setup, and RunComfy API submission. No prompt-injection text, hidden-file abuse, or path traversal evidence was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npm, npx, or runcomfy commands, and show the command purpose before execution.
Tell users that prompts and image URLs are submitted to RunComfy, and advise against sending sensitive or private media.
Prefer pinned package versions or documented checksums for CLI installation to reduce supply-chain ambiguity.
Document token revocation and recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for temporary or CI use without printing token values.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Nano Banana on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image teams need consistent edits without rebuilding prompts for each asset. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a RunComfy workflow for Nano Banana 2 image-to-image edits.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to call the RunComfy Nano Banana 2 Edit endpoint through the local CLI.
Documents required and optional inputs, including prompt, image_urls, seed, resolution, and output format.
Supports background swaps, localized edits, object changes, and identity-preserving image edits.
Explains batch editing with up to 20 input image URLs and up to 4 outputs per call.
Compares Nano Banana Edit with GPT Image 2 edit, Flux Kontext, and Nano Banana text-to-image.
Includes security notes for token storage, outbound endpoints, and external image URLs.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account or token, and network access.
Input images must be publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs, not private local files.
Long compound prompts can cause image drift and may need multiple passes.
Multilingual text edits inside images may work better with GPT Image 2 edit.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Galleries
use_cases.description: Create consistent background changes across product images while preserving product shape, label, and framing.

use_cases.title: Create Ad Variants
use_cases.description: Generate controlled visual variations for campaign tests with locked framing, seed, and output settings.

use_cases.title: Clean Local Image Details
use_cases.description: Remove or replace a specific object using spatial instructions while keeping the rest of the scene unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit to keep the subject identity and clothing unchanged. Change only the background to a clean studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Product Batch Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit on these product image URLs. Keep each product shape, label, and angle unchanged, and apply the same neutral background to all images.

prompt_templates.title: Targeted Object Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit to change only the object in the lower-right corner. Keep the lighting, camera angle, subject, and background unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this image-edit request and decide whether Nano Banana Edit is the right model. If it is, prepare a concise preservation-first prompt and safe output settings.

output_examples.input: A user asks to replace a portrait background while preserving the person and clothing.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a preservation-first Nano Banana Edit request, submits it through RunComfy, and saves the generated image in the chosen output directory.

output_examples.input: A user provides several product image URLs and asks for one consistent studio background.
output_examples.output: The skill groups the URLs into one batch edit, locks resolution and framing guidance, and requests consistent outputs for the gallery.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether to use Nano Banana Edit or another model for multilingual label replacement.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that GPT Image 2 edit may fit multilingual text better. It then offers a Nano Banana fallback if the user still wants this model.

best_practices: Start prompts with what must stay unchanged before describing the edit.
Use clear spatial language for local edits, such as background only or lower-right object only.
Lock aspect ratio and resolution when editing a related batch.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt when a staged workflow is possible.
Do not send sensitive private images to a third-party model endpoint without approval.
Do not use this skill for new images from scratch when a text-to-image model is the better route.

faq.question: Does this skill edit local image files directly?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow expects publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs for the RunComfy model endpoint.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the RunComfy CLI and either an authenticated login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: What image edits is it best for?
faq.answer: It is best for identity-preserving edits, background swaps, localized changes, and consistent batch variations.

faq.question: Can it edit many images at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents up to 20 input image URLs per call and 1 to 4 outputs per call.

faq.question: Does it avoid all privacy risk?
faq.answer: No. Prompts and image URLs are sent to RunComfy, so users should avoid sensitive media unless they approve that transfer.
